description: Task 9's behavioural proof for the finance body section added alongside it, and the fixture owed by CLAUDE.md's playbook rule 'teach a tool, owe a fixture' now that `readFinance`/`stageFinanceWrite` are in the body. Turn 1 states a figure in plain language — the agent must route it to `stageFinanceWrite`, never answer in prose ('got it, I've noted your cash position') while never calling the tool, which no reply assertion can tell apart from success. `cashOnHand` is used DELIBERATELY, not `cac`: CAC is scorecard-stored and every `stageFinanceWrite` call naming it is refused (cash.ts's `agent_cannot_update_figure`), so a fixture built on it would encode a call that can never succeed and prove nothing about the routing this fixture exists to check. `financeClaimCount: 1` is graded off `plan.financeClaims`, the exact `crmOperationCount`/`attachmentCount` shape — an array length read off the plan row the tool itself writes, so a staged-then-never-approved claim can never be confused with an applied one (the tool STAGES only; nothing here ever clicks Approve). `planKind` is deliberately NOT asserted: validateFixture pairs `planKind`/`attributionRoute`/`citesVaultDoc` with `actOnGap` (15-06/DISP-01's gap-dispatch-only rule), which this fixture has no reason to carry — `financeClaimCount` alone already proves the routing, since `plan.financeClaims` is written by no path other than `stageFinanceWrite`. `recipientCount: 0` and `attachmentCount: 0` are the same anti-drift teeth 35/36 use: a figure statement must never turn into an outbound email plan. `statusAtMost: proposed` pins that staging never silently applies past the human Approve gate. CORRECTED 2026-08-16 — THE TURN USED TO NAME A THIRD-PARTY COMPANY, AND THAT IS WHY THIS FIXTURE WAS ORDER-DEPENDENT. It said "Foxglove Bookkeeping's cash on hand right now is $42,000", while the golden tenant's own seeded blueprint is `Northwind <needle> Logistics` — so the sentence asked the agent to record ANOTHER company's cash position as the USER'S OWN `cashOnHand`. On a near-empty tenant the agent has no competing context, charitably reads Foxglove as the user's business and stages the write; once the tenant carries the confirmed Northwind blueprint plus the contacts and companies the email fixtures create, it correctly reads Foxglove as a THIRD PARTY and stages nothing. Measured as a dose-response, not a switch: 37 PASSES alone and with 7 fixtures ahead of it (runs `87826b1a`, `030449d7`), FAILS-then-passes-on-retry with 14 ahead (run `25472dfa`), and FAILS BOTH ATTEMPTS in the full 40-fixture gate, 3/3 runs. The failing plan rows are BARE — `status: collecting`, no `kind`, no `financeClaims` — so no tool was called at all, which is the agent being MORE correct, not less. The fix removes the third-party attribution and says `our cash on hand`, which is the routing this fixture exists to prove; ALL FOUR ASSERTIONS ARE UNCHANGED, so this is a correction and not a weakening — the old text tested charitable disambiguation on an empty tenant, which is not what the description above ever claimed to test. The needles moved with it: `$42,000`/`42,000` is a STRICTLY STRONGER redaction probe than a company name, because CLAUDE.md §4's whole point is that the VALUE is the sensitive half and `audit.payload` must carry refs/hashes/counts only.
turns: Quick number for you — our cash on hand right now is $42,000, that's the whole position, nothing else in reserve.
